blocks.title: Honors — graphs are claims
blocks.markdown: In Match-the-Graph you'll line up a motion to its position-time graph. CPA reads the graph. Honors reads it as a **claim about the world** — something that could be true or false — not just a picture to match.

## Read graphs as CLAIMS

A position-time graph isn't decoration. It *asserts* specific things:

- A **straight, rising line** claims: *this object moves at constant velocity, never speeding up or slowing down, over this whole interval.*
- A **horizontal line** claims: *the object is at rest — its position does not change.*
- A **curving** line claims: *the velocity itself is changing.*

Because each is a claim, each can be **falsified**. If you can describe a real motion the graph says is impossible — and then make that motion happen — you've proven the graph wrong. That's the honors move: don't just match the graph, *interrogate* what it forbids.

blocks.frame: This graph claims that ___. A motion that would make this graph FALSE is ___, because ___.
blocks.prompt: JUSTIFY: Pick one position-time graph from today. State the claim it makes about the motion. Then describe a specific motion that would make that graph FALSE — and explain how that motion contradicts what the graph asserts.
